# Typed charset queries keep different failure and compatibility contracts

GetCharsetLangGroup first resolves a charset alias and returns its failure before classification. It maps UTF-7 for lookup and preserves selected x-unicode results before using EncodingToLang. IsMultiByteCharset instead returns a Boolean: null and unknown labels are false, with an explicit UTF-7 fallback, while known labels use the inverse of IsSingleByte. MimeEncoder uses that Boolean in its existing non-main-body text/directory Base64 condition. The new tests list selected language groups and positive/negative classifications, including newly positive GBK/GB18030 and UTF-16 cases. Commented-out entries are not assertions, and the alias rejection of replacement is separate from other typed queries. No fresh codec, MIME or unit-test execution.

Scope: mailnews-charset.
